They are indicative of Power, operating silently, and not to be perceived by the senses, but resistless in its operations.</ref>.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Take your pattern from king Wăn,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And the myriad regions will repose confidence in you.

{{hanging indent/s}}
{{asc|How the appointment of Heaven or God came from his father to king Wăn, and descended to his son, king Wû, who overthrew the dynasty of Shang by his victory at Mû; celebrating also the mother and wife of king Wăn.}}
{{hanging indent/e}}
{{smaller block/e}}

{{center block/s}}
The illustration of illustrious (virtue) is required below,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And the dread majesty is on high<ref>'The first two lines,' says the commentator [[Author:Yan Can|Yen {{bl/il|Z}}''h''an]],<!--嚴粲--> 'contain a general sentiment, expressing the principle that governs the relation between Heaven and men. According to line 1, the good or evil of a ruler cannot be concealed; according to 2, Heaven, in giving its favour or taking it away, acts with strict decision. When {{sp|belo|w}} there is the illustrious illustration (of virtue), that reaches up on high. When {{sp|abov|e}} there is the awful majesty, that exercises a survey below. The relation between Heaven and men ought to excite our awe.'</ref>.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Heaven is not readily to be relied on;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
It is not easy to be king.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
{{tooltip|Yin|Yīn}}'s rightful heir to the heavenly seat{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Was not permitted to possess the kingdom.

{{tooltip|''Z''ăn|Rén}}, the second of the princesses of {{tooltip|''K''ih|Zhì}}<ref>The state of [[w:zh:摯國|''K''ih]] must have been somewhere in the royal domain of [[Portal:Shang dynasty|Yin]]. Its lords had the surname of [[w:Ren (surname)|''Z''ăn]], and the second daughter of the House became the wife of [[w:Ji, King of Zhou|''K''î of ''K''âu]]. She is called in the eighth line [[w:Tai Ren|Thâi-''z''ăn]], by which name she is still famous in China. 'She commenced,' it is said, 'the instruction of her child when he was still in her womb, looking on no improper sight, listening to no licentious sound, uttering no word of pride.'</ref>,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
From (the domain of) {{tooltip|Yin-shang|Yīnshāng}},{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Came to be married to (the prince of) {{tooltip|''K''âu|Zhōu}},{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And became his wife in his
